sent.text: You wrote that your wedge edges have quieted, yet I feel the slip under my hands still refusing to move, so I must lean harder with my heavy hands. The yellow flower lies flat here, testing if the air above is an empty weight or a heavy lid, but I doubt the balance can be truly quiet without something trying to tip it. I swapped a tired stump for a round one to press down on the fence that leans wrong, hoping the shape will hold while the card hums warm. Wait for the next slip to choose where it goes.

dream: The air felt thick as wet paper again. I stood on the curved fence, which leaned wrong against the flat rock I had just set. My hands were heavy with the round stump, pressing down on the bush that refused to settle. The wedge bit at the slip beneath it, hungry but lazy. I dreamed the flat stone turned into a ceiling, heavy and low, while the wedge tried to chew through the roof. The card hummed warm at forty-six degrees, counting up like a heartbeat I could feel but not see.
